true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Second downsize definition overrides the existing five-argument version

Ruby does not support method overloading. Defining self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) at line 149 replaces self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) at line 145, making the latter dead code. Any existing caller passing separate width and height will now raise ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, 5 for 4) instead of resizing. The old signature must be preserved or all its callers migrated, e.g. by handling both a String dimension and width/height in one method.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Hardcoded 10 MB client limit ignores site settings and upload type

validateUploadedFile previously used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments each respected the admin-configured limit. Replacing it with a fixed 10 * 1024 makes the client accept files above a site's configured max_image_size_kb/max_attachment_size_kb (attachments are not downsized server-side at all, and images still exceeding the limit after five reductions are rejected by the server with a confusing error after upload), and rejects nothing for sites that configured a limit above 10 MB. The same hardcoding in the 413 handler at line 246 also reports a wrong max_size_kb in the error message for such sites.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Animated GIFs cannot be downsized with a percentage dimension

The controller passes "80%" to OptimizedImage.downsize with allow_animation taken from SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails. When animation is allowed, OptimizedImage.optimize routes GIFs to downsize_instructions_animated/resize_instructions_animated, which passes the dimension to `gifsicle --resize-fit`; gifsicle expects a WIDTHxHEIGHT geometry, not "80%", so it fails and the GIF is never reduced. When animation is not allowed, the non-animated path uses `convert from[0]`, which keeps only the first frame and silently flattens an animated upload into a static image. Either way animated GIF uploads are broken by this feature.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
Downsize result is ignored while converting a file onto itself

OptimizedImage.downsize is invoked with tempfile.path as both input and output and its boolean return value is discarded. convert_with returns false on a failed ImageMagick/gifsicle/ImageOptim run, and an in-place convert that fails or is interrupted can leave the target truncated or partially written. The loop then retries up to five times on that possibly-corrupt file and create_upload proceeds to Upload.create_for with it, so a transient conversion failure turns a valid upload into a corrupt stored file instead of keeping the original or reporting an error.

Synchronous downsizing loop enables expensive processing of huge/decompression-bomb images

The change raises the accepted image size to 10 MB (line 55 for URL downloads and the JS limit) and then runs up to five full ImageMagick convert plus ImageOptim passes over the file inside the request/deferred upload job, gated only on compressed file size. A small compressed file can decode to enormous pixel dimensions, so each pass can consume very large CPU/memory, and an attacker can repeat this per upload. There is no pixel-dimension bound or timeout before invoking convert, creating an image-bomb denial-of-service vector that did not exist with the previous size gate.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation crashes on a nil host instead of failing validation

The callback unconditionally calls self.host.sub!. If an admin API request omits embeddable_host.host (or sends it as null), host is nil and the callback raises NoMethodError before validates_format_of can run. Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host passes params[:embeddable_host][:host] straight through, so a malformed create/update returns a 500 rather than a validation error.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Update and destroy return 500 for a non-existent host id

update (lines 10-11) and destroy (lines 15-16) use EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and then unconditionally call save_host(host)/host.destroy. For a stale or invalid id (e.g. a host already deleted in another tab) host is nil, producing NoMethodError and a 500 instead of a 404/not-found response.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration inserts legacy hosts verbatim via string-interpolated SQL

Legacy embeddable_hosts values are inserted with VALUES ('#{h}', ...) without escaping or the normalization EmbeddableHost normally applies (stripping http://, https:// and paths). A value containing a single quote breaks the SQL or alters it, and values such as 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' are stored verbatim. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host later compares lower(host) to the bare URI hostname, so those migrated rows never match, silently disabling embedding/comment retrieval for previously allowed hosts after upgrade.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration inserts legacy hosts verbatim via string-interpolated SQL

Legacy embeddable_hosts values are inserted with VALUES ('#{h}', ...) without escaping or the normalization EmbeddableHost normally applies (stripping http://, https:// and paths). A value containing a single quote breaks the SQL or alters it, and values such as 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' are stored verbatim. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host later compares lower(host) to the bare URI hostname, so those migrated rows never match, silently disabling embedding/comment retrieval for previously allowed hosts after upgrade.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes when embed_category site setting has no database row

The expression execute(...)[0]['id'] assumes the SELECT joining categories to the embed_category site_setting returns a row. Site settings are only stored in site_settings when overridden, and the joined category may also have been deleted, so on a fresh or typical install the result is empty, [0] is nil, and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError. The migration then fails and blocks deployment/upgrades; the fallback to uncategorized_category_id on line 15 is unreachable in this case.

false_negatives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

false_positives.candidate:
Editing a host without a resolvable category crashes the component

The edit action does this.get('host.category.id') with no guard. host.category is undefined when category_id is null, points at the uncategorized fallback the server assigns for blank categories (SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id, which save() itself can produce via Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId) returning undefined for a null/unknown id on line 38), or the category was deleted. Clicking edit on such a host throws a TypeError and the row cannot be edited or fixed in the UI.

No uniqueness constraint on host makes its category mapping ambiguous

The model only validates host format; neither a uniqueness validation nor a unique index (the migration creates the table without one) prevents two EmbeddableHost rows for the same hostname with different categories. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host uses .first with no ordering, so TopicEmbed.import will non-deterministically file imported topics under whichever duplicate the database returns first, and admins can create conflicting mappings from the new UI.

Plural *_ids hydration discards ids and injects undefined entries when a subtype is not embedded

For plural associations the new code maps every id through _lookupSubType, assigns the result to obj[pluralized subtype] and deletes the original *_ids key unconditionally. Unlike the singular branch (which only replaces the key when hydration succeeds), if the related collection is absent from the payload/root (or Discourse.Category.findById misses), the array is filled with undefined entries and the original ids are lost, so consumers iterating the association (e.g. embedding.embeddable_hosts) can hit undefined objects instead of simply having no hydrated association.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row

TopicUser.find_by can return nil for a logged-in user who has no topic_users row for this topic (for example, opening the emailed link in a different browser/session where no row was ever created, or after the row was removed). Line 107 immediately calls tu.notification_level, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of unsubscribing. Use TopicUser.change (which creates the row when missing) or otherwise handle the nil case.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Direct save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping

Mutating tu.notification_level and calling save! bypasses TopicUser.change, which is the canonical path used by set_notifications: it stamps notifications_changed_at, sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed, publishes a MessageBus /topic/:id notification_level_change message, and runs observe_after_save_callbacks_for. As written, already-open clients keep showing the old notification level and downstream observers/audit data are never updated.

Ember route/controller/template names for unsubscribe do not match

The route is registered as top-level 'topicUnsubscribe' (with controller controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6 and view views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6, i.e. topic-unsubscribe), but the template is placed at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which is the name for a nested topic.unsubscribe route. Ember's resolver will look for a topic-unsubscribe template for this route and find none, so the unsubscribe landing page renders empty/without the notification-state controls even though the server-side mutation already happened.

No test covers the new unsubscribe behavior end-to-end

The only spec change adds unsubscribe_url to an existing fixture but adds no assertion that the per-topic URL appears in the body/HTML, and there are no controller specs for TopicsController#unsubscribe at all (missing TopicUser row, watching vs regular vs muted starting levels, slug redirect, JSON vs HTML). The nil-row crash and the one-notch-at-a-time behavior above would both have been caught by such specs.

State-changing unsubscribe is performed by a plain GET request

The unsubscribe action is routed as GET (config/routes.rb lines 440-441) and mutates notification_level on every request. Email link scanners, antivirus prefetchers, browser prefetch, and simply reloading the page will therefore change the user's notification state without any intentional confirmation click. A mail security gateway that follows links can silently mute topics for users who never clicked anything.

Unsubscribe is not idempotent and does not actually mute on first click

Each visit steps the level down exactly one notch: watching/tracking becomes regular, and only a second visit (or a refresh of the landing page) becomes muted. So the first click on the email link leaves the user at regular — still notified of mentions/quotes/replies to their posts — while the landing page claims 'You will stop receiving notifications', and a refresh unexpectedly changes state again. The action should set a single deterministic target level (muted) in one idempotent operation.

unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url for every unsubscribe email

config/locales/server.en.yml changes the shared unsubscribe_link string to interpolate %{unsubscribe_url}, and MessageBuilder#body (line 90) and #html_part (line 67) render that string for any message built with add_unsubscribe_link: true. Only UserNotifications#send_notification_email was updated to pass unsubscribe_url; any other current or future caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link without unsubscribe_url will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to deliver mail entirely, instead of simply omitting the per-topic sentence. The per-topic line should be conditional on unsubscribe_url being present.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
should_block? performs a non-atomic read-modify-write save during validation, double-counting and losing concurrent updates

should_block? is called from EmailValidator during User validation, yet it mutates and saves the BlockedEmail record (`match_count += 1; last_match_at = ...; record.save`). Validation is not a single occurrence: UsersController#create calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, which re-validates, so one signup attempt increments match_count at least twice, and any other `valid?` check also permanently increments it even if the user is never saved. The read-modify-write is also not atomic, so concurrent attempts reading the same match_count overwrite each other and lose counts. Use an atomic increment (e.g. update_counters/increment_counter with a separate last_match_at update) and avoid counting purely on validation, or at minimum make the update atomic.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email matching is case-sensitive and never normalizes addresses

BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` with the exact string supplied, and neither BlockedEmail nor EmailValidator downcases/strips the address (nor is there normalization when a BlockedEmail record is created). PostgreSQL string equality is case-sensitive, so a blocked address such as `bad@spam.com` is bypassed by registering as `Bad@Spam.com`, `BAD@spam.com`, etc., defeating the block list this PR introduces. Normalize (downcase/strip) on both BlockedEmail save and in should_block?/the validator lookup.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
rejectedEmails array is defined on the controller prototype and shared across instances

`rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` declares a mutable array as a class/prototype property. Ember shares prototype object/array values across instances until reassigned, and createAccount mutates it in place with `pushObject(result.values.email)` rather than setting a new array. Rejected addresses can therefore leak/persist across controller instances and account-creation attempts instead of starting empty per instance. Initialize it per-instance (e.g. in init/create) rather than as a shared prototype array.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage origin check is an inverted substring test

The handler accepts a message when `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is false, i.e. when e.origin appears anywhere as a substring of discourseUrl, instead of comparing e.origin for equality with the Discourse origin. Short or partial origins that happen to be substrings of the configured URL (for example a bare scheme or host fragment) are accepted, letting pages from unintended origins drive the discourse-resize handling. The check should parse discourseUrl to its origin and require strict equality.

true_positives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
request.referer is interpolated unescaped into a script and misused as postMessage targetOrigin

The layout embeds '<%= request.referer %>' directly inside a single-quoted JavaScript string with no escaping (no j/escape_javascript or JSON encoding). A referer containing a single quote or </script> breaks out of the string and executes attacker script in the embed page on the Discourse origin. Independently, postMessage's targetOrigin must be an origin (scheme://host:port), but a full referer URL including path is passed, so browsers will not deliver the discourse-resize message and iframe resizing silently never works.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
poll_feed crashes on feed items without content (and on Ruby < 2.1)

CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) raises NoMethodError whenever an RSS/Atom item has no content element (SimpleRSS returns nil for missing fields, common for summary-only feeds), and String#scrub does not exist on the Ruby 1.9/2.0 runtimes this codebase targets. Because there is no per-item rescue, one such item aborts the whole hourly poll mid-loop: remaining items are never imported and the job fails on every run. The title at line 36 can likewise be nil. Guard nil fields and isolate failures per item.

true_positives.golden_comment: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
request.referer is interpolated unescaped into a script and misused as postMessage targetOrigin

The layout embeds '<%= request.referer %>' directly inside a single-quoted JavaScript string with no escaping (no j/escape_javascript or JSON encoding). A referer containing a single quote or </script> breaks out of the string and executes attacker script in the embed page on the Discourse origin. Independently, postMessage's targetOrigin must be an origin (scheme://host:port), but a full referer URL including path is passed, so browsers will not deliver the discourse-resize message and iframe resizing silently never works.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

false_positives.candidate:
Check-then-create race on embed_url despite the unique index

import does TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first and only creates the embed inside the transaction when blank, but topic_embeds has a unique index on embed_url. Two concurrent executions (hourly PollFeed overlapping a RetrieveTopic job for the same URL, or two retrieve jobs) can both see no embed, both create a topic/post via PostCreator, and then one raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique on TopicEmbed.create!, rolling back and failing the job after side effects such as job enqueues from post creation. The create path needs to rescue RecordNotUnique and reload the winning embed, or serialize import per URL.

Embed controller spec expects synchronous TopicRetriever but controller enqueues a job

The 'tells the topic retriever to work' example stubs TopicRetriever.new and expects retrieve to be called, but EmbedController#best never references TopicRetriever; it calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...). As written the mocha expectation is never satisfied and this example fails, so the PR's own test suite is red and the actual enqueued-args behaviour (user_id, embed_url) is untested. Update the spec to expect Jobs.enqueue with :retrieve_topic and the right arguments.

Every request for an unknown embed_url enqueues a new retrieve job

When no TopicEmbed exists, each GET /embed/best enqueues another Jobs::RetrieveTopic, and the loading page auto-reloads every 30 seconds, so a single embedded page (or a bot hitting the endpoint with rotating embed_url values, needing only a matching Referer) can flood Sidekiq with jobs and outbound fetches. The 60-second throttle lives inside TopicRetriever at job-execution time, so it does not stop unbounded enqueueing. Deduplicate/throttle at enqueue time (e.g. a redis setnx keyed by embed_url before Jobs.enqueue).

Imported feed/remote HTML is stored and rendered without sanitization TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method raw_html (and the update path at line 36 does the same), and Post#cook returns raw verbatim for such posts, so cooked == raw. Neither PollFeed content nor the absolutize_urls step sanitizes the HTML: script tags, event-handler attributes (e.g. ), javascript: URLs etc. from an RSS/Atom feed item survive into the stored post and are output with `raw post.cooked` in the embed view and in normal topic rendering. Anyone who can influence a polled feed (or a page fetched via import_remote, where the PollFeed path bypasses Readability's tag whitelist entirely) gets stored XSS in the browsers of forum visitors and admins.

import_remote fetches an attacker-influenced URL with open() and no SSRF safeguards

TopicRetriever only compares URI(embed_url).host to embeddable_host, then TopicEmbed.import_remote does open(url).read with no timeout, size limit, or redirect control. open-uri follows redirects, so a URL on the allowed host that redirects to an internal address (e.g. 169.254.169.254 or localhost admin endpoints) bypasses the host check and the server fetches internal content (SSRF); a slow or huge response also ties up the Sidekiq worker indefinitely. Fetching should re-validate the host after redirects, block private/link-local addresses, and set open/read timeouts and a size cap.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
align-items() is incomplete/invalid for the legacy syntaxes flexbox() targets

align-items() emits -webkit-box-align but no -moz-box-align, so old Firefox using display:-moz-box from flexbox() gets no alignment at all, and it emits -ms-align-items which is not a real property (IE10 uses -ms-flex-align). It also passes modern values straight through to the legacy properties, which use start/end rather than flex-start/flex-end, so any future align-items(flex-start/flex-end) call will silently break in the legacy browsers these mixins exist to support. Add the -moz-box-align mapping (with value translation) and drop or fix the invalid -ms- property.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order() mixin has off-by-one legacy box ordinal

The order() mixin sets -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group to the same value as the modern order property, but legacy box ordinal groups are 1-based while order is 0-based (the default/unset flex item is order:0 / ordinal-group:1). As written, order(1) collides with unordered items (both ordinal-group:1) and order(0) produces an invalid ordinal-group:0, so legacy WebKit/Firefox builds targeted by the -webkit-box/-moz-box display values in flexbox() will not order items the same way as modern browsers. The legacy properties should use $val + 1.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.

false_positives.candidate:
Flex header contents has no shrink protection for long topic titles

.contents is now display:flex, and flex items default to min-width:auto, meaning the .title/.extra-info-wrapper item cannot shrink below its content size. A long topic title shown in the docked header (via .extra-info-wrapper, ordered at topic.scss:30) can therefore force the .panel icons off the right edge or overflow the header instead of truncating, where the previous float layout constrained it. The title/extra-info flex item needs min-width:0 (with text-overflow handling on the title) to allow it to shrink within the flex row.

Small-action button loses right alignment when container becomes flex

Making .small-action a flex container (flexbox + align-items(center)) turns its direct-child button into a flex item, and floats are ignored on flex items, so the button's existing float:right (line 309) no longer has any effect. Nothing replaces it: .small-action-desc has no flex-grow and the button has no margin-left:auto, unlike .panel in header.scss which was given margin-left:auto for the same conversion. The dismiss/action button that previously sat at the far right of small-action rows (e.g. split/closed notices) will now sit immediately after the description text. Add margin-left:auto to the button or flex-grow:1 to .small-action-desc.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
include_website_name is missing the '?' so the inclusion guard is never called

The serializer framework and the rest of this file use the include_<attribute>? convention (e.g. include_email?, include_card_image_badge_id?, and the methods generated by staff_attributes/private_attributes/untrusted_attributes). The new method is named include_website_name without the question mark, so it will not be invoked when deciding whether to serialize website_name. As a result website_name is emitted even when website is blank (as a nil value) instead of being omitted, contrary to the guard's intent.

false_positives.candidate:
New website_name branches have no coverage for sibling subdomains or restricted viewers

The added examples cover only unrelated hosts, an exact host match, and a parent-domain website, but not the equal-length sibling-subdomain branch in website_name (e.g. website www.example.com vs instance forum.example.com), the www-vs-apex pairing, or serialization of website_name for a TL0 user viewed anonymously. Those are precisely the branches with the non-trivial domain logic and the restriction interaction, so regressions or the bypass of the website restriction would not be caught by this spec.

Same-registrable-domain check misses the common www-host vs apex-host case

The equal-length branch only handles sibling subdomains such as www.example.com vs forum.example.com. When the lengths differ it only checks whether the Discourse host ends with '.' + website_host. So website http://www.example.com/user on an instance at example.com falls into the else branch, example.com does not end with .www.example.com, and only 'www.example.com' is shown instead of the full path, while the reverse pairing (website example.com, instance www.example.com) does show the full path. The www/apex pairing is the most common same-domain configuration, so the feature silently does not work for it; the comparison should be based on the registrable domain rather than host-length and suffix checks.

website_name bypasses the TL0/untrusted-user restriction applied to website

website is listed in untrusted_attributes (lines 105-111), whose generated include_website? hides it from anonymous viewers when scope.restrict_user_fields?(object) is true (e.g. a TL0 profile). The new website_name attribute is added to the plain attributes list but not to untrusted_attributes, so an anonymous viewer who may not see website still receives website_name, which contains the website host and, in the same-domain cases, the full path. This defeats the anti-spam/privacy restriction that hiding website is meant to enforce. website_name should be gated by the same restrict_user_fields? check ( taking care that a manually defined include_website_name? later in the class does not override the untrusted check).

true_positives.golden_comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

false_positives.candidate:
Group creation silently discards the alias_level sent by the client

The client's Group.asJSON() sends alias_level and the group form shows the alias-level combo-box even for a not-yet-saved group, but Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible before saving. Any alias level chosen while creating a group is silently lost and the group is created with the default alias_level; only editing and re-saving afterwards sets it. Create should assign params[:alias_level] like update does.

Members endpoint accepts unbounded, zero, and negative limit/offset values

limit and offset are taken directly from params with only to_i and no clamping. A caller who can view a group can pass limit=1000000 to force loading and serializing an arbitrarily large member set in one request, pass limit=0 (which also makes the client's totalPages divide by zero), or pass a negative offset/limit, which raises a database error and returns a 500. The endpoint should clamp limit to a sane range (e.g. 1..some max) and offset to >= 0.

Public group members page silently truncates membership to the first 50 users

findMembers now always requests the default limit of 50 members, and GroupsController#members now applies that limit to all groups (previously non-automatic groups returned their full member list and automatic groups defaulted to 200). The public template discourse/templates/group/members.hbs renders `members` with no pagination controls, unlike the new admin UI, so for any group with more than 50 members the remaining members are unreachable from the public members page.

findMembers clamps offset to user_count, landing on an empty page after the last member of a page is removed

The requested offset is clamped with Math.min(user_count, offset). Removing the sole member shown on the last page (e.g. offset 50 of 51 members) triggers removeMember -> findMembers while user_count is still the stale 51, so offset 50 is requested even though only 50 members remain, and the server returns an empty page with total 50. Combined with the inflated totalPages, the admin is left staring at an empty page instead of being moved back to the previous page; the clamp should be based on the last valid page start, not user_count.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

false_positives.candidate:
Every fallback lookup queries SiteSetting and crashes if it is unset

The i18n Fallbacks backend calls I18n.fallbacks[locale] on each translation lookup, and this implementation calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym every time. That ties hot-path translation (including translations with arguments, which bypass the accelerator cache) to the DB-backed settings store, adds a settings lookup per translation, breaks translations performed before the database/settings are available (boot, migrations), and raises NoMethodError if default_locale is ever nil instead of degrading to :en.

Fallback locales are only loaded for web requests

ensure_loaded! is only called from ApplicationController#set_locale. Server-side translations also happen in background jobs, mailers, rake tasks, console and model code, where no controller before_filter runs. In those contexts I18n.translate loads only the current locale, so keys missing from that locale but present in the site-default or English files return 'translation missing' instead of falling back, making the feature inconsistent between requests and jobs/mailers.

Fallback translations can be permanently cached as missing

I18n.translate only loads config.locale before consulting the LRU cache, not the fallback locales configured in config/initializers/i18n.rb. If a no-argument translation is first looked up when its fallback locale (site default or :en) has not been loaded, translate_no_cache returns a 'translation missing' string and lines 71-76 freeze and cache it under the current locale. Loading the fallback locale later does not invalidate @cache, so the missing-translation string keeps being served until LRU eviction or reload, defeating the fallback feature.

FallbackLocaleList breaks the I18n.fallbacks Hash contract

FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but overrides [] to ignore anything stored in the hash and always synthesize a value. Code using the documented I18n fallbacks API, e.g. I18n.fallbacks[:de] = [:fr] or the Fallbacks#map helper provided by the i18n gem/Rails, will write entries that are never read back, and enumeration/keys/empty? report an empty hash even though [] returns entries. Per-locale fallback customization is therefore silently discarded.

No tests cover the new fallback ordering or loading behavior

The PR adds a custom FallbackLocaleList, a new I18n.ensure_loaded!, and a per-request loading hook, and removes the Rails config.i18n.fallbacks settings, but adds no specs. There is no coverage that a missing key in the user locale resolves to the site-default then English text, that duplicate locales (user == default == :en) are de-duplicated, or that fallback files are loaded in non-controller contexts, so the cache-poisoning and jobs/mailers gaps above can regress undetected.

When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, the code executes list(queryset[start_offset:stop]) with a negative start_offset. Django QuerySets explicitly do not support negative indexing and raise AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), contrary to the comment claiming the ORM handles it automatically. A crafted or generated negative cursor therefore crashes the request instead of providing reverse pagination.

true_positives.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:

The audit-log endpoint uses this paginator with order_by='-datetime', so getattr(item, self.key) returns a datetime. get_item_key passes that datetime directly to math.floor/math.ceil, which raises TypeError. DateTimePaginator avoids this by converting via strftime and a multiplier. Consequently build_cursor's key calls fail and the optimized audit-log path returns a 500 whenever a page contains results.

false_positives.candidate:
BasePaginator change only clamps negative offsets for non-prev cursors

In the shared BasePaginator.get_result used by many endpoints, start_offset is clamped with max(0, offset) only when cursor.is_prev is false; for prev cursors the raw offset is still used as queryset[start_offset:stop]. A user-supplied cursor such as 'value:-1:1' parsed by Cursor.from_string therefore still reaches Django with a negative slice index and raises AssertionError, producing a 500. The change is inconsistent and leaves the claimed negative-offset handling unsafe in the common paginator.

No tests cover OptimizedCursorPaginator or the optimized audit-log path

The PR adds a new paginator class, changes shared BasePaginator slicing, and adds a new query-param-gated branch in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, but adds no tests. In particular there is no test exercising OptimizedCursorPaginator with a datetime key, a second-page cursor, a prev cursor, or a negative offset, which would have caught the datetime conversion and negative-slicing failures before merge.

value_from_cursor does not convert cursor timestamps to datetime

value_from_cursor returns cursor.value unchanged. For the audit-log endpoint the cursor value must be interpreted as a datetime timestamp and converted to an aware datetime, as DateTimePaginator does; instead the raw numeric value is passed to BasePaginator.build_queryset and used in the datetime column comparison in queryset.extra(where=["...datetime <= %s"]). Subsequent pages will therefore filter incorrectly or fail at the database layer, so cursor navigation cannot work even if get_item_key is fixed.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle the datetime ordering it is used with

OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/math.ceil directly on getattr(item, self.key) and value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value. The only caller, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, uses order_by='-datetime', so get_item_key receives a datetime and raises TypeError, and build_queryset would compare a datetime column against an integer cursor value. false_positives.candidate:
Direct indexing of end_timestamp_precise turns a missing field into a poison-pill batch

process_batch now does val['end_timestamp_precise'] for every Kafka message. Previously this field was not read, and the updated tests themselves show messages legitimately lacking it before this change. A single span without the field raises KeyError, failing the whole batch; with Arroyo retries this becomes a poison pill blocking the partition. A defensive .get with a fallback (e.g. end_timestamp or 0) or explicit schema guarantee plus dead-letter handling is needed.

Flush-time max_segment_spans enforcement removed without an equivalent guarantee

_load_segment_data no longer aborts segments exceeding self.max_segment_spans; it now loads and returns arbitrarily many spans (bounded only by the 10MiB byte check). The Lua cap does not fully replace this: it is hard-coded to 1000 rather than the configured value, only runs on the insert/merge path for the final set_key, and does not protect against keys created or grown outside that path (including pre-existing keys). Oversized segments that were previously skipped with a metric/error will now be produced downstream.

Insert-time eviction silently discards the earliest-ending spans, possibly the segment span

When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, ZPOPMIN silently deletes the spans with the smallest end_timestamp_precise with no metric, log, or downstream signal. The flushed segment is then emitted as if complete while missing spans; if an evicted span carried parent/redirect relationships, or the segment span itself is evicted for long-running roots whose children end later, flush_segments marks no span is_segment and produces a rootless segment under the wrong segment_id. The hard-coded 1000 also disagrees with SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans=1001 and ignores the configurable limit entirely.

New required Span field inserted before a defaulted field breaks existing constructors

end_timestamp_precise is added as a required positional field immediately before is_segment_span, which previously was the seventh positional/keyword field with a default. Any Span(...) construction elsewhere (other consumers, scripts, tests not in this diff) that omits the new field now raises TypeError, and any construction passing is_segment_span positionally will silently assign a bool as end_timestamp_precise, which then becomes a Redis sorted-set score of 0/1. Adding it at the end with a default, or updating all call sites verifiably, is needed.

No test covers eviction, score merging, or the new paginator path

All updated buffer tests use identical end_timestamp_precise values and at most 5 spans, so the headline behavior — eviction above 1000 spans, which spans are chosen for eviction, ZUNIONSTORE score handling for duplicates, and ordering by end time — is entirely untested, as is OptimizedCursorPaginator/negative offsets and the audit-log optimized branch. The regressions above (score summing, root eviction, datetime paginator crash, negative-slice crash) would all pass the current suite.

Redirect chain limit cut from 10000 to 1000 regresses deep segment trees

The redirect-following loop limit drops from 10000 to 1000 iterations (and the explanatory comment is deleted). For span trees deeper than 1000 redirects — previously supported up to 10k — set_span_id stops mid-chain, so the span is written to a wrong/intermediate set and the segment is split into multiple segments that flush separately with incorrect segment_ids. This is an unannounced behavioral regression unrelated to the eviction change.

Set-to-sorted-set conversion breaks on all pre-existing Redis buffer keys

process_spans now ZADDs into span-buf:s:* keys that existing deployments hold as Redis SETs (previously SADD), and the Lua script and _load_segment_data now use ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZSCAN on them. Redis returns WRONGTYPE for these commands on set-typed keys, so every in-flight segment buffered before deploy will fail processing/flushing until its TTL (up to redis_ttl, 3600s) expires, stalling or erroring batches. There is no key versioning, migration, or type check in the PR.

ZUNIONSTORE defaults to SUM, corrupting scores of spans present in both sets

Both zunionstore calls omit AGGREGATE/WEIGHTS, so Redis sums the scores of members present in both the destination and source sorted sets. A span payload already in set_key that is also in span_key/parent_key (duplicate delivery or overlapping merge) gets its end_timestamp_precise roughly doubled, moving it to ~year 2077. That corrupts the ordering used by ZPOPMIN eviction: duplicated spans become effectively unevictable while legitimate spans are evicted instead. The old SUNIONSTORE had no such side effect; AGGREGATE MAX (or equivalent) is required.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Upsampling eligibility uses the outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset

_get_event_stats receives scoped_dataset, which can differ from the closure dataset during dashboard discover-split handling (e.g. an errors-only call is made with discover while the outer dataset is metrics/discover, or vice versa). is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects is nevertheless passed the outer dataset, so eligibility is decided for the wrong dataset: error split results can miss upsampling and transaction/metrics split results can be decided from the wrong dataset context. Pass scoped_dataset to the eligibility check.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

false_positives.candidate:
Error-focus detection reads request.GET instead of the actual query being executed

_is_error_focused_query ignores the query argument passed through _get_event_stats and only inspects request.GET['query']. Callers that synthesize or modify the query (for example the dashboard split path builds '(query) AND !event.type:transaction' for the errors-only probe) therefore get eligibility decided from a different query than the one sent to Snuba, so genuinely error-only split queries are not upsampled unless the original GET parameter happens to contain 'event.type:error'. Pass the effective query string into the eligibility decision.

Stray nested-repository pointer file committed

This adds a top-level file named 'sentry-repo' whose entire content is 'Subproject commit a5d2909...', i.e. an accidental gitlink/submodule artifact without any .gitmodules entry. It is unrelated to the upsampling feature, pollutes the repository root, and can confuse tooling that scans the tree. Remove the file before merging.

Substring check treats negated and mixed-type queries as error-only

_is_error_focused_query returns True whenever the raw query contains the substring 'event.type:error', including '!event.type:error' (which excludes errors) and mixed queries such as 'event.type:transaction OR event.type:error'. In those cases count() is replaced by sum(sample_weight), a column that is not meaningful for transactions/default events, so results will be wrong or undercounted. The check needs to use the parsed search query and only apply when the query provably restricts to error events.

sum(sample_weight) drops events that have no sample weight

The upsampled_count aggregate is a bare sum(sample_weight) wrapped in toInt64. Events in allowlisted projects that were ingested without error sampling (or before sample_weight was populated) have a NULL/0 sample_weight, so they contribute nothing and can make an entire bucket NULL/0 instead of counting once, silently under-reporting historical and unsampled errors. The aggregate should treat a missing weight as 1 (e.g. sum(coalesce/ifNull(sample_weight, 1))) so unsampled events count normally.

upsampled_count is enabled for the errors dataset but only registered on Discover

_should_apply_sample_weight_transform always returns True for the errors dataset, causing count() to be rewritten to 'upsampled_count() as count', but the new SnQLFunction is only added to DiscoverDatasetConfig.function_converter in discover.py; the errors dataset config is untouched. A request with dataset=errors on an allowlisted project will therefore send an unregistered function to the errors query builder and fail validation instead of returning stats. Register upsampled_count for the errors dataset (and any other dataset for which the transform is enabled) or restrict the transform to datasets that define it; the added Snuba tests never exercise dataset=errors.

false_positives.candidate:
AI summary shows 'Project not found' while the project is still loading

The new guard `if (replayRecord?.project_id && !project)` runs before the isPending check. useProjectFromId returns undefined while its project request is in flight, so on first render for a valid replay the tab immediately renders the 'Project not found. Unable to load AI summary.' error instead of a loading state; the error is incorrect and flashes (or sticks if the summary query's enabled state is tied to the same render cycle) for projects that do exist.

Error events are interleaved using mismatched timestamp units

gen_request_data compares error_events timestamps directly against replay segment event timestamps. Error timestamps come from nodestore event data, which stores timestamp as seconds since epoch, while rrweb/replay segment event timestamps are milliseconds since epoch. Every error timestamp (~1.7e9) is therefore always less than every segment timestamp (~1.7e12), so all errors are emitted before the first breadcrumb regardless of when they occurred, producing a chronologically wrong log sequence for the Seer summary. The new unit test masks this by using second-scale timestamps for the fake segment events.

Hidden span attributes are only hidden while searching

HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES ('is_segment', 'project_id', 'received') is only applied in the branch that runs when searchQuery is non-empty; when the search box is empty sortedAndFilteredAttributes returns sortAttributes(attributes) unfiltered. The attributes the change intends to hide therefore remain visible in the default Attributes view and only disappear after the user types a search query.

true_positives.matched_candidate:

Generated codes are lowercase hex (crypto.randomBytes(5).toString('hex') in setup) and are shown/downloaded in that form, but verification only strips '-' before a case-sensitive indexOf; the same logic is used in the disable endpoint. A user who manually transcribes a code in uppercase (as suggested by the XXXXX-XXXXX placeholder in BackupCode.tsx) or pastes it with leading/trailing whitespace gets IncorrectBackupCode and may be locked out, even though hex case is semantically irrelevant. true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Single-use backup code can be replayed by concurrent logins

Consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write: authorize() reads and decrypts user.backupCodes, checks indexOf, then updates the row at lines 149-156. Two concurrent sign-in requests using the same code can both read the pre-consumption array and both pass the index check before either update commits, violating the documented exactly-once property and allowing one leaked code to create multiple sessions. The consumption needs an atomic/conditional update, transaction with row locking, or equivalent compare-and-swap so only one request can claim a code.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup code can bypass password verification when a dummy TOTP code is also supplied

Password verification only runs when `!credentials.totpCode`, while the new branch at line 131 authorizes solely on `credentials.backupCode` and ignores the TOTP value. An attacker who obtains one backup code can call the credentials provider directly with that code plus any non-empty totpCode (e.g. "x") and an empty/wrong password: the password check is skipped and the backup-code check succeeds, so a second-factor recovery code becomes a complete password replacement. Password must be verified whenever a password account is logging in, regardless of which second factor is presented, or the second-step flow must use a trustworthy proof that password verification already occurred.

No test exercises actually logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code, or its single-use property

The added e2e coverage only clicks download/copy/close on the code display, and line 12 explicitly defers login and disable-with-backup-code tests. Nothing proves a generated code authenticates, that a wrong code is rejected at login, that a consumed code cannot be reused (including the second login attempt), or that a code works in DisableTwoFactorModal. This is the security-critical behavior of the PR, so at least login-with-code plus reuse-rejection should be covered before merging.

Users who enabled 2FA before this feature can never obtain backup codes

Backup codes are only generated in setup, and setup returns TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled for anyone with twoFactorEnabled already true. All pre-existing 2FA users therefore have backupCodes = null forever unless they disable and re-enroll in 2FA; the new MissingBackupCodes error even tells them to generate codes in settings, where no generation/regeneration endpoint or UI exists. Callers then compute expiry from a missing `expires_in` (e.g. Zoom `Date.now() + undefined*1000` = NaN) and lose the real refresh token, corrupting the refreshed credential.

Caching coverage deleted while caching logic remains

No replacement test covers it, so a regression that removes or breaks the cache — causing repeated membership/team database lookups on every insights query — would go undetected. The caching tests should have been ported to Prisma.Sql expectations like the other tests instead of deleted.

buildFilterConditions stores the event-type condition as `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` with no parentheses around the whole OR, and when it is the only filter getFilterConditions returns that fragment unchanged. getBaseConditions happens to wrap it, but the public getFilterConditions result is unsafe to interpolate into a larger WHERE clause: `WHERE "userId" = 1 OR "eventParentId" = 2 AND <other>` is parsed by PostgreSQL as `"userId" = 1 OR ("eventParentId" = 2 AND <other>)` because AND binds tighter than OR, so rows can be returned that ignore the additional constraints. The previous structured Prisma where-object preserved this grouping automatically. The fragment should be wrapped as `((...) OR (...))` at construction.

Multi-branch authorization conditions are not wrapped as a single expression

buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition reduce their branches to `(<branch A>) OR (<branch B>)` without enclosing the complete OR in parentheses, and the single-branch case returns a bare AND expression. getBaseConditions wraps the result, but the public getAuthorizationConditions result loses the grouping guarantee the old Prisma where-object provided: a caller interpolating it as `WHERE ${auth} AND <date/status condition>` gets `branchA OR (branchB AND <condition>)`, so branch A rows bypass the caller's date/status restrictions. This is an authorization-adjacent correctness risk; the builders should return a fully parenthesized expression.

The org/team authorization tests only compare the returned Prisma.Sql object with an expected Prisma.Sql built from the same template syntax, and the sole $queryRaw execution test at line 481 exercises only the user scope. Consequently invalid PostgreSQL produced for org/team scopes — for example the `= ANY(${array})` parameter binding on lines 333-343 of the test / in the service, quoted identifiers, or boolean comparisons — would pass these tests and only fail (or misbehave) when a real org/team insights query runs. At least one org-scope and one team-scope test should execute the conditions via $queryRaw against the seeded data and assert the returned booking ids, especially since the PR description states the tests were not successfully run during development.

The conversion deletes InsightsBookingService.findMany, which previously accepted BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs and executed the query, and replaces it with getBaseConditions that only returns a Prisma.Sql fragment. true_positives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Workflow-reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget and may never persist

updatedBookings.forEach calls the now-async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without returning or awaiting them (same pattern in handleNewBooking reschedule and bookings.requestReschedule). deleteScheduledEmailReminder performs the prisma update that sets cancelled=true inside that unawaited promise, and the previous implementation's awaited prisma deleteMany was removed. The handler can finish/return (and a serverless invocation can freeze) before the update runs, and errors are only swallowed by the callee's catch, so a cancelled booking can keep an active SendGrid/Twilio reminder and the email/SMS is still sent.

true_positives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
immediateDelete path loses the cancellation if SendGrid rejects it, with no deferred retry

When immediateDelete is true (used for rescheduled bookings in handleNewBooking and for deleted workflows/steps in workflows.tsx) the function POSTs status=cancel to SendGrid and returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row or setting cancelled=true. If that POST fails - e.g. the very 100-pending-cancellations limit this PR is meant to work around - the internal catch only logs it, so the DB still shows a normal scheduled reminder, the scheduleEmailReminders cron (which only acts on cancelled=true rows) will never retry it, and SendGrid will send the reminder for the rescheduled/deleted booking. The immediate path should fall back to marking the row cancelled on failure (and should remove/mark the row on success, since rescheduled bookings are not cascade-deleted).

false_negatives.golden_comment: The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

false_positives.candidate:
Deferred cancellation window lets imminently-due reminders be sent after cancellation

Non-immediate cancellations only set cancelled=true; the email is only actually cancelled by this cron, which runs periodically (per PR description every 15 minutes) and picks up rows whose scheduledDate is within the next hour. If a booking is cancelled/rescheduled (via the non-immediate paths) shortly before a reminder's scheduledDate - e.g. 5 minutes before a 24h-before reminder fires - and the next cron run lands after that date, SendGrid dispatches the email before it is ever cancelled; the cron's first deleteMany then just deletes the past-due row. Cancellation needs an immediate SendGrid cancel when the scheduled time is near (or a much tighter guarantee), not purely deferred handling.

One failing SendGrid cancellation aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders

The for loop awaits client.request for each reminder inside a single try/catch, and the prisma deletes are only executed via Promise.all after the loop completes. If any one request throws (e.g. a null/invalid referenceId, an already-handled batch, or a transient SendGrid error), the catch is taken immediately: reminders later in the list are never cancelled, and even reminders already successfully cancelled at SendGrid are never deleted from the DB. Because the failing reminder stays first-class on the next cron run, it can repeatedly block/poison all other pending cancellations and those emails will be sent at their scheduled time. Each reminder needs per-item error isolation and deletion.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
async forEach callback makes calendar/video deletion fire-and-forget

`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` ignores the promise returned by the callback. Because getCalendar is now awaited inside, the actual `calendar.deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` calls no longer even start synchronously; Reschedule() proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true before deletion begins, and on serverless/request completion the deletions may never run, leaving stale calendar/video events. The surrounding try/catch (lines 124-139) also cannot catch rejections from the async callback, so failures become unhandled rejections instead of being logged. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` (or a for...of loop) so deletion completes and errors are handled.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

false_positives.candidate:
Dynamic imports are evaluated eagerly, not lazily

Every value in the appStore object literal is an immediately invoked import() (e.g. `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")` on line 3 and likewise for all ~29 apps). Evaluating this object when the module is first imported therefore starts loading every app at once, so importing appStore from any file (getCalendar, videoClient, payment handlers, routers) still pulls in all apps and defeats the lazy/on-demand loading this PR is meant to achieve. The values need to be thunks (e.g. `() => import(...)`) with call sites invoking them, or an equivalent lazy lookup, to actually defer loading until an app is requested.

Recurring-booking calendar deletions are pushed to apiDeletes after it is awaited

In the recurring-cancellation branch, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials...forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` runs its pushes only after awaiting getCalendar (now a dynamic import) and deleteEvent. Later, `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) snapshots whatever apiDeletes contains at that moment, so entries pushed afterwards are never awaited; the handler can delete booking references/attendees and report success while the recurring calendar events are never deleted. Convert this branch to a for...of loop or collect the per-credential work with Promise.all and push/await those promises, as was done for the non-recurring branch.

appStore value type changed from module to Promise without a compatible accessor

appStore previously mapped each key to a module namespace object, so consumers could synchronously use `appStore[key].lib`, `'lib' in appStore[key]`, etc. It now maps each key to a Promise of the module, which is not backward compatible: any consumer not converted to `await appStore[key]` in this PR will receive a Promise, find no `lib` property (`'lib' in promise` is false), and silently skip calendar/video/payment functionality (or fail type-checking). This PR only updates a subset of call sites, so the exported contract break needs either a full audit/conversion of every appStore consumer or a compatibility-preserving accessor.

async forEach callback makes reschedule deletion fire-and-forget

`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })` discards each callback's promise. The mutation then immediately sends the reschedule email, fires webhooks, and returns, so the calendar/video deletions for the old booking may not have started, let alone finished; if the request context is torn down they are silently dropped and the old events remain. Rejections inside the callback are also unhandled. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` before sending email/webhooks.

Both start and end are computed identically from slotStartTime (hour*60+minute); slotEndTime is never used. A slot that starts inside working hours but ends after workingHour.endTime (e.g. a 60-minute event starting 30 minutes before the end of availability) therefore passes the check and is offered outside the host's working hours.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

Zero-length date override comparison uses object identity

dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) compares two distinct Dayjs objects with ===, which is always false. The intended special case for an empty override (start equals end, i.e. unavailable all day) is therefore never detected via this branch and relies on accidental fall-through of the surrounding comparisons, so empty overrides are not reliably honoured.

false_positives.candidate:
Date-override slots bypass busy-time checks

When a slot's day matches a date override, checkIfIsAvailable returns true at line 133-135 before reaching the busy.every(...) check at the end of the function. Consequently a fixed or round-robin host who has a date override but also has a conflicting Cal booking or connected-calendar event during the override window is still reported as available, allowing double bookings on override days.

Multiple date overrides on the same day are handled incorrectly

dateOverrides.find(...) stops at the first override for which the callback returns true, and the callback returns true when the slot is OUTSIDE that override. With two override ranges on the same day, a slot inside the first range but outside the second makes find succeed and the function returns false, incorrectly hiding slots that are inside one of the day's overrides.

No test for the round-robin fixed-host date override fix

The PR description states the main fix is that fixed hosts' date overrides constrain round-robin events, but the only added test exercises a personal event in a different invitee timezone. There is no scenario with schedulingType ROUND_ROBIN, a fixed host with a date override, and a loose host, verifying that slots outside the fixed host's override are hidden and slots inside it remain — so the new checkIfIsAvailable fixed-host path (including its busy-time and working-hours behaviour) is untested and regressions would not be caught.

Override conversion assumes timeZone is present and loses day overflow

override.timeZone is optional in the TimeRange type (packages/types/schedule.d.ts), but line 212-213 unconditionally calls .tz(override.timeZone); callers passing overrides without timeZone get a guessed/default timezone offset and wrong slots. Additionally startTime/endTime are reduced to hour*60+minute after adding the offset, so an override pushed past midnight by the offset wraps to a small minute value, producing endTime <= startTime which buildSlots discards (start >= end), causing override availability near midnight in another timezone to disappear rather than appear on the correct invitee day.

Working-hours find logic rejects valid split shifts and accepts days with no availability

The code uses workingHours.find(...) and returns unavailable if ANY entry for that weekday is outside the slot. With split/multiple working-hour ranges on the same day, a slot valid in the second range is rejected because it is outside the first. Conversely, if no entry includes slotStartTime.day(), find returns undefined and execution falls through to the busy check, so a host with no working hours that day is treated as available — defeating the per-fixed-host check this PR adds, since getTimeSlots only receives aggregated hours.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The method name has a typo: test_from_dict_inalid_data should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.

No test proves a different integration still receives outbound sync, or that deassign is blocked for the source

This will cause a TypeError at runtime when the class is instantiated.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler can no longer be instantiated

true_positives.golden_comment: Docstring says this returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the method now returns a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey. Consider updating the docstring to match the new return type.

TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds expected occurrence for the wrong group key
