Rejected addresses can therefore leak/persist across controller instances and account-creation attempts instead of starting empty per instance. It also passes modern values straight through to the legacy properties, which use start/end rather than flex-start/flex-end, so any future align-items(flex-start/flex-end) call will silently break in the legacy browsers these mixins exist to support. Add the -moz-box-align mapping (with value translation) and drop or fix the invalid -ms- property.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order() mixin has off-by-one legacy box ordinal

The order() mixin sets -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group to the same value as the modern order property, but legacy box ordinal groups are 1-based while order is 0-based (the default/unset flex item is order:0 / ordinal-group:1). As written, order(1) collides with unordered items (both ordinal-group:1) and order(0) produces an invalid ordinal-group:0, so legacy WebKit/Firefox builds targeted by the -webkit-box/-moz-box display values in flexbox() will not order items the same way as modern browsers. The legacy properties should use $val + 1.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments point to the same problem. The legacy box-ordinal-group properties are 1-based while order is 0-based, so passing $val directly is wrong, and a value of 0 is invalid. The candidate also notes that order(0) gives an invalid ordinal-group:0 and suggests using $val + 1.

Making .small-action a flex container (flexbox + align-items(center)) turns its direct-child button into a flex item, and floats are ignored on flex items, so the button's existing float:right (line 309) no longer has any effect. Nothing replaces it: .small-action-desc has no flex-grow and the button has no margin-left:auto, unlike .panel in header.scss which was given margin-left:auto for the same conversion. true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
include_website_name is missing the '?' so the inclusion guard is never called

The serializer framework and the rest of this file use the include_<attribute>? convention (e.g. include_email?, include_card_image_badge_id?, and the methods generated by staff_attributes/private_attributes/untrusted_attributes). The new method is named include_website_name without the question mark, so it will not be invoked when deciding whether to serialize website_name. As a result website_name is emitted even when website is blank (as a nil value) instead of being omitted, contrary to the guard's intent.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate flags the same core problem as the golden comment: include_website_name is missing the '?' suffix, so the conditional inclusion guard is never invoked. It does not mention the secondary string-mutation point, but the primary issue matches.

false_positives.candidate:
website_name bypasses the TL0/untrusted-user restriction applied to website

website is listed in untrusted_attributes (lines 105-111), whose generated include_website? hides it from anonymous viewers when scope.restrict_user_fields?(object) is true (e.g. a TL0 profile). The new website_name attribute is added to the plain attributes list but not to untrusted_attributes, so an anonymous viewer who may not see website still receives website_name, which contains the website host and, in the same-domain cases, the full path. This defeats the anti-spam/privacy restriction that hiding website is meant to enforce. website_name should be gated by the same restrict_user_fields? check ( taking care that a manually defined include_website_name? later in the class does not override the untrusted check).

Same-registrable-domain check misses the common www-host vs apex-host case

The equal-length branch only handles sibling subdomains such as www.example.com vs forum.example.com. When the lengths differ it only checks whether the Discourse host ends with '.' + website_host. So website http://www.example.com/user on an instance at example.com falls into the else branch, example.com does not end with .www.example.com, and only 'www.example.com' is shown instead of the full path, while the reverse pairing (website example.com, instance www.example.com) does show the full path. The www/apex pairing is the most common same-domain configuration, so the feature silently does not work for it; the comparison should be based on the registrable domain rather than host-length and suffix checks.

New website_name branches have no coverage for sibling subdomains or restricted viewers

The added examples cover only unrelated hosts, an exact host match, and a parent-domain website, but not the equal-length sibling-subdomain branch in website_name (e.g. website www.example.com vs instance forum.example.com), the www-vs-apex pairing, or serialization of website_name for a TL0 user viewed anonymously. Those are precisely the branches with the non-trivial domain logic and the restriction interaction, so regressions or the bypass of the website restriction would not be caught by this spec.

request.referer is interpolated unescaped into a script and misused as postMessage targetOrigin

The layout embeds '<%= request.referer %>' directly inside a single-quoted JavaScript string with no escaping (no j/escape_javascript or JSON encoding). A referer containing a single quote or </script> breaks out of the string and executes attacker script in the embed page on the Discourse origin. Independently, postMessage's targetOrigin must be an origin (scheme://host:port), but a full referer URL including path is passed, so browsers will not deliver the discourse-resize message and iframe resizing silently never works.

Because there is no per-item rescue, one such item aborts the whole hourly poll mid-loop: remaining items are never imported and the job fails on every run. The title at line 36 can likewise be nil. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate: Imported feed/remote HTML is stored and rendered without sanitization TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method raw_html (and the update path at line 36 does the same), and Post#cook returns raw verbatim for such posts, so cooked == raw. Neither PollFeed content nor the absolutize_urls step sanitizes the HTML: script tags, event-handler attributes (e.g. ), javascript: URLs etc. from an RSS/Atom feed item survive into the stored post and are output with `raw post.cooked` in the embed view and in normal topic rendering. Anyone who can influence a polled feed (or a page fetched via import_remote, where the PollFeed path bypasses Readability's tag whitelist entirely) gets stored XSS in the browsers of forum visitors and admins.

import_remote fetches an attacker-influenced URL with open() and no SSRF safeguards

TopicRetriever only compares URI(embed_url).host to embeddable_host, then TopicEmbed.import_remote does open(url).read with no timeout, size limit, or redirect control. open-uri follows redirects, so a URL on the allowed host that redirects to an internal address (e.g. 169.254.169.254 or localhost admin endpoints) bypasses the host check and the server fetches internal content (SSRF); a slow or huge response also ties up the Sidekiq worker indefinitely. Fetching should re-validate the host after redirects, block private/link-local addresses, and set open/read timeouts and a size cap.

Every request for an unknown embed_url enqueues a new retrieve job

When no TopicEmbed exists, each GET /embed/best enqueues another Jobs::RetrieveTopic, and the loading page auto-reloads every 30 seconds, so a single embedded page (or a bot hitting the endpoint with rotating embed_url values, needing only a matching Referer) can flood Sidekiq with jobs and outbound fetches. The 60-second throttle lives inside TopicRetriever at job-execution time, so it does not stop unbounded enqueueing. Deduplicate/throttle at enqueue time (e.g. a redis setnx keyed by embed_url before Jobs.enqueue).

Check-then-create race on embed_url despite the unique index

import does TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first and only creates the embed inside the transaction when blank, but topic_embeds has a unique index on embed_url. Two concurrent executions (hourly PollFeed overlapping a RetrieveTopic job for the same URL, or two retrieve jobs) can both see no embed, both create a topic/post via PostCreator, and then one raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique on TopicEmbed.create!, rolling back and failing the job after side effects such as job enqueues from post creation. The create path needs to rescue RecordNotUnique and reload the winning embed, or serialize import per URL.

Embed controller spec expects synchronous TopicRetriever but controller enqueues a job

The 'tells the topic retriever to work' example stubs TopicRetriever.new and expects retrieve to be called, but EmbedController#best never references TopicRetriever; it calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...). As written the mocha expectation is never satisfied and this example fails, so the PR's own test suite is red and the actual enqueued-args behaviour (user_id, embed_url) is untested. Update the spec to expect Jobs.enqueue with :retrieve_topic and the right arguments.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

Defining self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) at line 149 replaces self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) at line 145, making the latter dead code. Any existing caller passing separate width and height will now raise ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, 5 for 4) instead of resizing. The old signature must be preserved or all its callers migrated, e.g. by handling both a String dimension and width/height in one method.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

validateUploadedFile previously used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments each respected the admin-configured limit. Replacing it with a fixed 10 * 1024 makes the client accept files above a site's configured max_image_size_kb/max_attachment_size_kb (attachments are not downsized server-side at all, and images still exceeding the limit after five reductions are rejected by the server with a confusing error after upload), and rejects nothing for sites that configured a limit above 10 MB. The same hardcoding in the 413 handler at line 246 also reports a wrong max_size_kb in the error message for such sites.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Animated GIFs cannot be downsized with a percentage dimension

The controller passes "80%" to OptimizedImage.downsize with allow_animation taken from SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails. When animation is allowed, OptimizedImage.optimize routes GIFs to downsize_instructions_animated/resize_instructions_animated, which passes the dimension to `gifsicle --resize-fit`; gifsicle expects a WIDTHxHEIGHT geometry, not "80%", so it fails and the GIF is never reduced. When animation is not allowed, the non-animated path uses `convert from[0]`, which keeps only the first frame and silently flattens an animated upload into a static image. Either way animated GIF uploads are broken by this feature.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate describes the same problem as the golden comment: the 80% dimension is passed to gifsicle --resize-fit on the animated path, which expects WxH geometry, so the downsize fails. The extra point about flattening frames does not change the match.

false_positives.candidate:
Downsize result is ignored while converting a file onto itself

OptimizedImage.downsize is invoked with tempfile.path as both input and output and its boolean return value is discarded. convert_with returns false on a failed ImageMagick/gifsicle/ImageOptim run, and an in-place convert that fails or is interrupted can leave the target truncated or partially written. The loop then retries up to five times on that possibly-corrupt file and create_upload proceeds to Upload.create_for with it, so a transient conversion failure turns a valid upload into a corrupt stored file instead of keeping the original or reporting an error.

Synchronous downsizing loop enables expensive processing of huge/decompression-bomb images

The change raises the accepted image size to 10 MB (line 55 for URL downloads and the JS limit) and then runs up to five full ImageMagick convert plus ImageOptim passes over the file inside the request/deferred upload job, gated only on compressed file size. false_positives.candidate:
One failing SendGrid cancellation aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders

The for loop awaits client.request for each reminder inside a single try/catch, and the prisma deletes are only executed via Promise.all after the loop completes. If any one request throws (e.g. a null/invalid referenceId, an already-handled batch, or a transient SendGrid error), the catch is taken immediately: reminders later in the list are never cancelled, and even reminders already successfully cancelled at SendGrid are never deleted from the DB. Because the failing reminder stays first-class on the next cron run, it can repeatedly block/poison all other pending cancellations and those emails will be sent at their scheduled time. If a booking is cancelled/rescheduled (via the non-immediate paths) shortly before a reminder's scheduledDate - e.g. 5 minutes before a 24h-before reminder fires - and the next cron run lands after that date, SendGrid dispatches the email before it is ever cancelled; the cron's first deleteMany then just deletes the past-due row. Cancellation needs an immediate SendGrid cancel when the scheduled time is near (or a much tighter guarantee), not purely deferred handling.

async forEach callback makes calendar/video deletion fire-and-forget

`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` ignores the promise returned by the callback. Because getCalendar is now awaited inside, the actual `calendar.deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` calls no longer even start synchronously; Reschedule() proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true before deletion begins, and on serverless/request completion the deletions may never run, leaving stale calendar/video events. false_positives.candidate:
Dynamic imports are evaluated eagerly, not lazily

Every value in the appStore object literal is an immediately invoked import() (e.g. `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")` on line 3 and likewise for all ~29 apps). Evaluating this object when the module is first imported therefore starts loading every app at once, so importing appStore from any file (getCalendar, videoClient, payment handlers, routers) still pulls in all apps and defeats the lazy/on-demand loading this PR is meant to achieve. The values need to be thunks (e.g. `() => import(...)`) with call sites invoking them, or an equivalent lazy lookup, to actually defer loading until an app is requested.

appStore value type changed from module to Promise without a compatible accessor

appStore previously mapped each key to a module namespace object, so consumers could synchronously use `appStore[key].lib`, `'lib' in appStore[key]`, etc. It now maps each key to a Promise of the module, which is not backward compatible: any consumer not converted to `await appStore[key]` in this PR will receive a Promise, find no `lib` property (`'lib' in promise` is false), and silently skip calendar/video/payment functionality (or fail type-checking). This PR only updates a subset of call sites, so the exported contract break needs either a full audit/conversion of every appStore consumer or a compatibility-preserving accessor.

async forEach callback makes reschedule deletion fire-and-forget

`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })` discards each callback's promise. The mutation then immediately sends the reschedule email, fires webhooks, and returns, so the calendar/video deletions for the old booking may not have started, let alone finished; if the request context is torn down they are silently dropped and the old events remain. Rejections inside the callback are also unhandled. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` before sending email/webhooks.

Recurring-booking calendar deletions are pushed to apiDeletes after it is awaited

In the recurring-cancellation branch, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials...forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` runs its pushes only after awaiting getCalendar (now a dynamic import) and deleteEvent. Later, `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) snapshots whatever apiDeletes contains at that moment, so entries pushed afterwards are never awaited; the handler can delete booking references/attendees and report success while the recurring calendar events are never deleted. Convert this branch to a for...of loop or collect the per-credential work with Promise.all and push/await those promises, as was done for the non-recurring branch.
